$comment: Normalization and path classification for compare-records.py (design-decisions D7 item 2, D14.6, D15).
STRUCTURAL. volatileKeyNames/volatileKeySuffixes replace a STRING value with <volatile>, so a
run-to-run clock is never reported as a contract change. Only string values are ever seen here:
the numeric twins of these keys (ticks, *Ticks, wallSeconds, *Us) are numbers and are classified
as readings by readingPathPatterns, so listing them here would declare a normalization that
never happens. endpointKeyNames keep the address of an endpoint and normalize only its port: a
ledger peer is the client's source address plus an OS-chosen ephemeral port, so the port changes
every run while a changed address still has to be reported. numericTextKeyNames rewrites only the
interpolated DECIMAL measurements inside prose notes (the F3 rates and F1 ceilings such as
40.191 requests/s or 203826.7 ms, which move every run), so the note template is still compared;
whole-number constants quoted in a note (the 256/16384 deferred queue bound, 4096 in-flight
window, 1048576 cap, RFC numbers) stay compared as literals.
conditionalPathPatterns list the paths a well-formed run may publish on one side only (a pure
TCP or pure UDP arm omits the other family's block; an empty histogram is omitted): they are
reported in column 2 and never fail the comparison. volatileArityPatterns list arrays whose
element count is data-dependent.
CLASSES (D15). identityPathPatterns are checked for presence and JSON kind only: a pid, an
ephemeral source port, the plan path and the version/hash keys differ per run by design. Path
keys live here rather than in a separate list so that exactly one mechanism means 'the value is
not compared'. readingPathPatterns are the measurement readings: clocks, CPU/memory/thread
gauges, throughput, transfer volumes and latency-histogram readings. Their movement is reported
for information and never fails. Everything else numeric is a contract value that must land
inside its per-key jitter band, so a counter cannot be silenced by omission (fail-closed).
latency/* is listed as a reading outright (D17.1): the histogram subtree is a sample aggregate,
and every statistic under it -- count included, which no *Us pattern matches -- moves with the
host rather than with the contract.
contractPathPatterns pins the declared plan inputs: parameters/* is what the plan asked for, not
a measurement, so a change there is a contract change even when the name ends in Bytes.
classOverrides carries the D15 item 6 cross-class key: gates/inFlightCeilingMs is a gates.*
counter by shape and a millisecond measurement by meaning, and it is classified a reading here
rather than by a pattern that happens to match it. A path matching both a contract and a reading
pattern is a configuration error, not a precedence rule; --explain-classes prints the rule that
classified every observed numeric path.
EVERY PATTERN IS A SPELLING THE RUN ACTUALLY PUBLISHES (D16.2). A pattern that matches no path
declares a shape the artifacts never carry, so the dead ones are gone rather than kept just in
case: the process gauges are top-level in a sample record (workingSetBytes, threads -- the */
variants matched nothing because nothing nests them under a slash), metrics/*Bytes already covers
every echoed or transferred volume (metrics/*bytesEchoed matched none of the echoedBytes forms),
the ledger's expectedBytes is top-level and has no tcp/ sibling, and the only lane ARRAY is the
tcp one: the udp half is a single lane whose udp.laneStarted is a scalar, so metrics/udp.lane*
declared an array arity that cannot vary. The bare sources array is listed and needs no */ form.
